title: Staged Release Traffic Sculptor — wireframes & flow
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype a compact, developer-friendly Rollouts editor (codename: Traffic Sculptor) for Redwood Console that supports staged releases: percentage-based canary, multi-variant A/B experiments, and safe rollback. Focus is on a single unified flow that balances clarity for engineers with guardrails for less experienced PMs. Deliverables: interactive wireframes (Figma), interaction spec, accessibility checklist, and a short UI component inventory for implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive Figma wireframes cover: 1) Quick create canary (single slider), 2) Multi-variant A/B with weighted controls, 3) Manual JSON editor for advanced splits, 4) Rollback action and timeline view.
Design spec includes: form validation rules, error states, confirmation modal copy for destructive actions, and telemetry events mapping to backend API fields.
Usability test (n=6 engineers/PMs) shows median task time < 3 minutes to create a 10% canary with rollout schedule and no critical usability blockers.
Sign-off from PM (Jules Park) and Eng lead (Priya Rao) on guardrail behaviors and final visual mockups.
design_notes: Primary pattern: percentage slider with exact-value input and preset buttons (1%, 5%, 10%, 25%, 50%) to speed common tasks.
Secondary pattern: visual split canvas that shows traffic allocation across variants with color-coded preview and hover details showing example responses.
Support for deterministic routing keys for experiment seeding (expose 'seed by user id' toggle) to ensure consistent variant exposure.
Safety: require explicit graduation criteria and minimum observation window before auto-scale of canary to 100% (configurable), with suggested defaults curated by SRE.
Fallback UX: clearly surfaced automatic fallback plan (model variant or region fallback) that will be used on errors; allow user to select fallback strategy in the same flow.
